attendance: over 2,500 healthcare professionals (56th Annual Conference, Aurora CO, 24-27 Apr 2025)
attendance_method: A1 attempted first: the ASAM exhibitor/sponsor pages sit on eventscribe.net (annualconference.asam.org) and returned Cloudflare 403 to both WebFetch and curl with a browser UA, so no prospectus figure could be confirmed. Fell back to A3: loaded the Guideline Central post-conference recap of the 56th Annual Conference, which states in its opening paragraph 'Over 2,500 healthcare professionals attended the event.' Same page also says 'With over sixty sessions and more than 100 posters, there was a lot to take in.' Basis is UNSPECIFIED - the recap does not say whether the 2,500 is delegates only or includes exhibitor/industry staff. Trade-press rather than organiser, so treat as approximate.
ratio_rationale: Judged 5%, against EuroPCR 6% - the counted anchor for a meeting whose attendance is driven by taught content rather than submitted science. ASAM is a CME/clinical-practice conference for addiction physicians (workshops, courses, board-prep, policy plenaries); the contributed-science track is one poster session bolted onto it. The recap I loaded independently describes 'over sixty sessions and more than 100 posters', i.e. a poster hall roughly 4% the size of the headcount, which is what put me at the bottom of the anchor range rather than in the 20-40% research-society band.
programme_evidence: Guideline Central recap: 'With over sixty sessions and more than 100 posters' - session-led CME programme with a small poster track; ASAM conference schedule pages list courses, general sessions and one poster session.
direct_abstracts_note: 'more than 100 posters' on the Guideline Central recap - accepted/presented posters at the 2025 meeting, not submissions (submissions would be higher). Third-party source, not organiser.
character_evidence: https://www.guidelinecentral.com/insights/2025-asam-annual-conference-recap/ - posters and poster awards exist (so a call for abstracts exists), but they sit inside a predominantly invited/CME programme.

attendance_year: 2026 (forward-looking prospectus figure for the Oct 2026 Boston meeting; reads as the society's standing attendance claim)
attendance_method: Loaded the ASBMR Annual Meeting 'Exhibit' page (the exhibitor-facing pitch). It states '2,100+ registered attendees, including physicians, researchers and healthcare professionals from all over the world.' 'Registered attendees' is a headcount of registrations, so TOTAL_ONSITE rather than DELEGATES - it is not broken out against industry staff, and as an exhibitor-facing number it is a pitch, not a count. A search snippet elsewhere asserted 'more than 2,500 attendees from more than 40 countries' for ASBMR; I did not load a page carrying that sentence, so I am NOT reporting it as a figure, only flagging that a larger number circulates.
ratio_rationale: Judged 50%, against SOT 46% and ATS 50%. ASBMR is a single-discipline basic-and-translational research society meeting (bone and mineral metabolism) rather than a clinical-education congress: its audience is laboratory and clinical investigators who attend in order to present, and its programme is built around orals selected from submitted abstracts plus large poster sessions. That is the same shape as SOT and ATS, both counted near 50%, and unlike the 6-15% CME congresses. Caveat: the 2,100 is a registration headcount that includes exhibitor and industry staff, so the true delegate denominator is smaller and the real ratio is if anything higher than 50%.
programme_evidence: Exhibitor page frames the audience as 'physicians, researchers and healthcare professionals'; the meeting is the field's principal research forum. Note: I did not load a call-for-abstracts page for ASBMR, so this is a read of the meeting's shape, not quoted programme wording.
character_evidence: No call-for-abstracts or author-guidelines page was opened within budget. ASBMR is very likely CONTRIBUTED but I am not asserting it without a loaded page.

attendance_method: Loaded the ObesityWeek 'Attendee Profile' page, the organiser's own retrospective statistics page for sponsors. It states 4,403 total registrants for ObesityWeek 2025 (in-person), broken down by country - United States 3,202, Brazil 184, United Kingdom 97, across 60 countries - and '300+ scientific sessions'. Because the total is reconciled against a country-by-country breakdown it is a count, not a projection, hence A2 over A1. Basis TOTAL_ONSITE: registrants at the in-person meeting, but no split between delegates and exhibitor/industry staff is given, so the delegate denominator is somewhat smaller than 4,403. A search snippet elsewhere asserted 'more than 3,200 attendees' for ObesityWeek 2024; I did not load a page carrying it, so it is not recorded as a figure - note the 3,202 US registrants on the page I did load is suspiciously close to it.
ratio_rationale: Judged 30%, between EASL 24% and UEG 35% / ASN 35% - the counted band for a single-organ/single-disease society congress that mixes a large basic-and-clinical science programme with clinical practice content. ObesityWeek is The Obesity Society's scientific meeting run jointly with the surgical/clinical side, and the attendee-profile page I loaded lists 'Abstracts in Journal' and 'Abstract Submissions' as headline programme elements alongside 300+ sessions, i.e. submitted science is a first-class part of the meeting rather than a bolted-on poster hall. It sits below UEG/ASN because a meaningful share of the room is practising clinicians and allied health attending for education, and above the 6-15% CME congresses. Caveat: converting a registrant total that includes industry staff, so this is if anything an understatement per delegate.
programme_evidence: Attendee-profile page: '300+ scientific sessions', with 'Abstracts in Journal' and 'Abstract Submissions' listed as programme elements, against a clinician-heavy registrant mix across 60 countries.
direct_abstracts_note: The attendee-profile page references a downloadable statistics PDF that likely carries an abstract-submission count; not opened, per the brief's instruction not to hunt abstract counts.
character_evidence: https://obesityweek.org/support/attendee-profile/ - 'Abstract Submissions' and 'Abstracts in Journal' listed as standing programme elements of the meeting.

conference: ICEM — International Conference on Emergency Medicine
attendance: over 2,500 experts and academics from home and abroad (23rd ICEM, Taipei, 19-23 Jun 2024)
attendance_rung_name: official press release (Office of the President, Republic of China (Taiwan)) covering the opening ceremony
attendance_method: Loaded the Taiwanese presidential office's news release on President Lai attending the ICEM 2024 opening. It states 'Over 2,500 experts and academics from home and abroad have gathered here for this year's conference.' This is a host-government source independent of the organiser (between A3 and A4), quoting the opening address, so it is a round headline number rather than a reconciled registration count - basis UNSPECIFIED, with no delegate/industry split and no statement about virtual attendance. No organiser post-meeting report or exhibitor prospectus with a figure surfaced; icem24.com congress-information page was not opened within budget.
ratio_rationale: Judged 30%, against UEG 35% and EASL 24% - international multi-track congresses where a large free-paper/poster programme runs alongside substantial clinical education. The specific thing that pushed ICEM into that band rather than the 6-15% CME band is the queue note itself: the ICEM abstract supplement is CJEM 27(S1) at 234 printed pages, which is a large contributed volume for a 2,500-person meeting - on typical supplement density that is several hundred to ~1,000 abstracts, i.e. a materially higher share than any teaching-led congress would generate. ICEM is also a biennial global congress that draws emergency physicians and trainees who travel specifically to present, and trainee-heavy specialties submit at high rates. Caveat: the 2,500 is an unsplit headline, so the delegate denominator is smaller and this ratio is conservative.
programme_evidence: A peer-reviewed abstract supplement (CJEM 27(S1), pp. 1-234) exists for the meeting, indicating a substantial contributed free-paper/poster programme running alongside the invited international plenary programme described in the presidential news release.
character_evidence: Existence of the CJEM 27(S1) abstract supplement (234 pages) for ICEM implies an open call for abstracts; no call page was loaded within budget.

The NMA convention is a professional-association gathering: CME across 26 specialty sections, House of Delegates and governance business, awards, advocacy and career/networking programming, with a Scientific Assembly and an abstract/poster track running alongside rather than driving it. That is the same shape as AAD and ASHP - large clinical audiences attending for education and association business - and nothing like the 30-50% research-society meetings. It sits slightly above the 6% teaching-course floor because the meeting does brand itself a Scientific Assembly and runs an open abstract call with a strong resident/student presence, which lifts submission rates.

character_evidence: https://nmanet.org/convention26/ - an open 'Submit an Abstract' call exists, but inside a predominantly invited CME/association programme (hence HYBRID rather than CONTRIBUTED).

attendance: over 8,200 physicians, of whom 828 from outside the United States (New Orleans, 3-5 Apr 2025)
attendance_rung_name: society post-meeting report (ACP Global Engagement Update, May 2025)
attendance_method: Loaded ACP's own post-meeting highlights piece: 'Internal Medicine Meeting 2025 was held in New Orleans, Louisiana April 3-5 and had an attendance of over 8,200 physicians', with '828 attendees from outside the United States' and 'more than 200 sessions'. Basis DELEGATES - the figure is explicitly physicians, and ACP's meeting policies page states non-clinical company representatives may only attend as paid exhibitors/sponsors, so industry staff sit outside this count. Retrospective and from the society itself, so no discount needed. The page carries no abstract or poster figures.
ratio_rationale: Judged 7%, between EuroPCR 6% and AAD 9%. ACP Internal Medicine is the archetype of a meeting whose attendance says almost nothing about submitted science: practising general internists travel to it for board-relevant CME, clinical skills workshops and practice-management content - 'more than 200 sessions covering a wide variety of clinical and practice management topics' on the page I loaded, with the meeting's other headline being 300 new FACP credential recipients, i.e. recognition and association business. Its contributed science is real but structurally small and trainee-restricted: the abstract competitions are resident/medical-student poster tracks funnelled up from chapter meetings, not a general call across the 8,200 attending physicians. That puts it just above EuroPCR's pure-teaching floor and below AAD.
programme_evidence: ACP post-meeting report: 'more than 200 sessions covering a wide variety of clinical and practice management topics'; headline outcomes are CME and FACP credentialing, with no abstract or poster counts mentioned at all.
character_evidence: Resident/student abstract competitions exist alongside an otherwise invited CME programme; no general open call page was loaded within budget.

attendance: over 17,780 participants including physicians, researchers, policymakers and representatives from 140 countries (30th EHA Congress, Milan, 12-15 Jun 2025)
attendance_rung_name: post-congress report by a participating European Reference Network (EuroBloodNet)
attendance_method: Loaded EuroBloodNet's post-congress news item on EHA 2025, which states 'over 17,780 participants' and 'representatives from 140 countries', alongside 'more than 575 scientific presentations'. Basis UNSPECIFIED and this matters: EHA runs a large hybrid congress, and a search snippet (not loaded, so not recorded) asserts the 30th Congress had 'just over 17,000 attendees (15,000 in person in Milan)'. If that split is right, 17,780 is TOTAL_INC_VIRTUAL and the in-person delegate base is nearer 15,000, itself still including industry staff. I could not confirm the split on a loaded page. EHA's own 'congress by the numbers' page was not reached within budget.
ratio_rationale: Judged 25%, against WCLC 25% and EASL 24% - large international disease-area congresses of exactly this shape, where a very big submitted-abstract programme runs under an equally big industry-facing and clinical-education programme. EHA is the European haematology field's primary venue for first presentation of trial and translational data, so a substantial minority of the room is there because their work is on the programme; but it is also a congress with heavy pharma presence and thousands of practising haematologists attending purely to hear results, which is what keeps it well below the 35-50% research-society band. The queue's existing third-party '4,000+ submitted' figure would imply ~22% against this same headline, reached independently and consistent with where the anchors put me. REVISED under the updated brief: my first version called 25% 'the conservative end' because the 17,780 includes roughly 2,800 virtual attendees on the unconfirmed split. That reasoning is withdrawn - an abstract presented online is still an abstract, and EHA's hybrid attendees include presenters. 25% is now simply the number I believe, not a hedged floor. The one discount I would still apply if I could is industry booth staff, who cannot submit; EHA publishes no delegate/industry split, so I am converting a headline that contains them and cannot quantify by how much it is padded.
programme_evidence: 'more than 575 scientific presentations' at a congress of ~17,800 participants drawn from 140 countries - a large invited and selected-oral programme sitting on top of a much larger poster/abstract base, with a heavy industry and clinical-audience draw.
direct_abstracts_note: A snippet asserts EHA 'received over 4,000 submissions for oral and poster presentations' for 2025, matching the queue's existing third-party '4,000+ submitted'. Not recorded as a figure - I did not load a page carrying it, and per the brief I did not spend searches hunting it.
character_evidence: EHA runs an open annual call for oral and poster abstracts feeding the congress programme; no call page was loaded within budget, so this rests on the abstract-driven structure described in the loaded post-congress report.

attendance: 9,517 registrants (US 5,950 / 64%, International 3,567 / 36%), explicitly excluding meeting exhibitors
attendance_rung_name: exhibitor prospectus - but carrying a reconciled registration table, not a pitch number
attendance_method: Downloaded the ARVO 2026 Annual Meeting Exhibitor Prospectus PDF (curl with browser UA, 11MB) and read it with pdftotext. Under 'ARVO Meeting Registration' it gives a table: U.S. 5,950 (64%), International 3,567 (36%), Total 9,517 (100%), footnoted '*Total does not include meeting exhibitors'. That footnote is what makes this a DELEGATES basis and unusually clean for an A1 source - the society has deliberately stripped industry staff out of the number it sells to exhibitors. The same document gives 2025 attendees by region of residence, 75 countries, ~200 exhibitors, and a degree mix (PhD 30%, MD 23%). A search snippet also asserted '10,900+ attendees' at ARVO 2025; that sentence is not in the registration table I read, so it is not recorded - it is most likely the exhibitor-inclusive total, which would put industry staff at roughly 1,400.
ratio_rationale: Judged 60%, above ATS 50% and AAIC 50% and approaching GSA's 119%. ARVO is as close to a pure research meeting as medicine has: the prospectus's own degree mix is PhD 30% / MD 23%, the audience is laboratory and clinical vision scientists, there is no CME-for-practice draw (practising ophthalmologists go to AAO instead), and the meeting's entire structure is papers and posters selected from submitted abstracts. Meetings of that character sit at or above ATS/AAIC's 50%, and ARVO is more purely investigator-only than either, since ATS and AAIC both carry large clinical-education audiences that ARVO does not. Cross-check: the row's existing dated ~6,100 abstracts/yr (2007-2010), set against the 9,517 exhibitor-excluded registrants I confirmed, implies 64% - consistent with the judgement, and reached independently of it. The denominator here is already exhibitor-free, so no discount is needed.
programme_evidence: The prospectus states that a full-meeting exhibitor badge 'is not sufficient for presentation of an abstract' and that anyone presenting 'must also register as full meeting, non-exhibitor attendees' - the meeting polices the boundary between commercial attendance and abstract presentation precisely because presenting is the normal reason to be there.
character_evidence: ARVO-2026 prospectus (loaded) - abstract presentation rules and registration categories for presenters; ARVO runs an annual open call for abstracts.

attendance: 6,964 professional medical attendees actually attended (7,516 registered); separately 6,456 industry attendees, of whom 6,208 exhibitor staff - total onsite approximately 13,420
attendance_method: Found the link on https://www.aaos.org/annual/exhibit-sponsor/plan-your-exhibit/attendee-registration-numbers/ (WebFetch hit a TLS issuer error; fetched with curl and a browser UA) and downloaded the linked PDF, 'AAOS 2026 Annual Meeting Final Attendance Numbers, New Orleans', read with pdftotext. It gives registered-vs-attended for every category. Final Professional Medical: US Physicians 3,515/3,291, US Residents 1,024/963, International Physicians 1,416/1,316, International Residents 40/38, Other Healthcare Professionals 1,485/1,320, Physician Assistants 36/36, Total 7,516 registered / 6,964 attended. Final Industry: Exhibitor 6,516/6,208, Exhibitor R&D 45/44, Industry Non-Exhibitor 212/204, Total 6,773/6,456. Exhibit hall: 584 exhibiting companies, 186,200 sq ft. This is the best class of source in the ladder - a retrospective count the society publishes against its exhibitors, with attrition shown. I take 6,964 (professionals who actually attended) as the delegate figure.

alt_figures.note: 6,964 professional + 6,456 industry attended. Any headline citing ~13,000-14,000 for AAOS is this number; it is 48% industry staff and must not be converted.

ratio_rationale: Judged 30%, between SABCS 21% and UEG 35% / ASN 35%. AAOS is a genuine two-headed meeting: a very large instructional programme (instructional course lectures, surgical skills, symposia) that draws practising surgeons who never submit, running alongside one of the largest contributed paper-and-poster programmes in surgery, fed by an academic and resident base that submits heavily - the final attendance report shows 1,001 residents actually attended, and residents/fellows are the highest-submitting group in any surgical specialty. That mix puts it above the 9-12% pure-CME academies and below the 40-50% research societies. The critical discount is already applied: the headline anyone would otherwise quote is ~13,400 onsite, of which 6,456 are industry staff. Converting that would overstate the row by 93%; I convert only the 6,964 professional attendees.
programme_evidence: The final attendance report shows a professional body of 6,964 (including 1,001 residents and 1,354 international physicians and residents) against a 584-company, 186,200 sq ft exhibit floor - i.e. a large academic constituency inside a heavily commercial, heavily instructional meeting.
character_evidence: AAOS runs an open annual call for papers and posters alongside a large invited instructional-course programme; no call page was loaded within budget, so character rests on the meeting's known two-track structure rather than quoted wording.

attendance: over 3,000 delegates from all over the world (17th World Congress on Public Health, Rome, 2-6 May 2023)
attendance_rung_name: congress series' own retrospective congress-history page
attendance_method: Loaded the official WCPH congress-history page, which for the 17th congress (Rome 2023) states 'Over than 3000 delegates from all over the world attended.' No other edition on that page carries a figure. Basis DELEGATES - the word used is delegates, and this is a congress with a modest exhibition, so industry inflation is small. The congress is biennial, so 2023 is the most recent completed edition with a published number (the 18th, Cape Town, is 2026, with an expectation of 'over 2,000 delegates' that I did not confirm on a loaded page and therefore do not record). A2 rather than A3: retrospective and from the organiser.
ratio_rationale: Judged 50%, against ATS 50% and ECR 48%. A world congress on public health is structurally a submission-driven meeting: its programme is built almost entirely from contributed oral and poster sessions plus organised symposia that are themselves proposed by delegates, and its audience is overwhelmingly academics, ministry and NGO staff from around the world for whom an accepted abstract is the institutional justification (and often the funding condition) for the trip. That travel-on-acceptance dynamic is what puts it at the top of the anchor range with ATS and ECR rather than in the 20-30% clinical-congress band; there is no practising-clinician CME constituency attending purely to learn, as there is at UEG or EASL. Denominator is already a delegate count, so no discount applied.
programme_evidence: WCPH is an abstract-driven biennial world congress (contributed oral and poster sessions plus delegate-proposed symposia) rather than a taught CME programme; the congress-history page frames each edition by delegates and themes rather than courses.
character_evidence: Each WCPH edition runs an open international call for abstracts; no call page was loaded within budget, so this rests on the congress structure rather than quoted wording.

ARRS is a general-radiology CME meeting - its prospectus's own pitch is that 'this is the general radiology meeting radiologists want to attend' for quality of education, with a categorical course as a paid add-on - so much of the room is there to learn. But it is small and academically dense (35% of members practise in academic/research settings) and runs a real scientific paper and electronic-exhibit programme with its own published abstract collection, so submitters form a materially larger share of a 2,500-person meeting than they do of RSNA's 40,000+. I am genuinely torn on this row and the brief asks me to say so: a reading that weights the CME framing puts it near 15%, and a reading that weights the size of the e-poster and scientific-paper programme relative to a compact academic meeting puts it near 30%. 22% is the figure I find most likely. That reasoning is withdrawn - online attendees can and do present, so the virtual half of the headline is not padding and I am no longer marking the number down for it. I report attendance_numeric as 879, i.e. 1,010 minus the 131 industry/other, per the brief's instruction to discount an inflated headcount before converting; the full 1,010 headline is in alt_figures. Flagging one impurity in that discount under the updated brief's rule that only people who cannot submit at all should be removed: the category ASRA publishes is 'Industry/other', not 'exhibitor staff'. At a device-heavy regional-anesthesia meeting it is overwhelmingly booth personnel, which is why I discounted it, but the 'other' tail may contain a few people who could submit. The choice is immaterial to the outcome - at my ratio the two denominators give roughly 176 vs 202 - so if the orchestrator prefers the undiscounted 1,010 for consistency across rows, nothing is lost. The 346 trainees are NOT discounted: trainees submit more, not less. DISAMBIGUATION the orchestrator must resolve: ASRA runs TWO annual meetings - this Spring regional-anesthesia/acute-pain meeting (~1,010) and a separate autumn Annual Pain Medicine Meeting, which has its own prospectus and its own, different attendance. ratio_rationale: Judged 20%, against SABCS 21% at the top and ASHP 12% at the bottom, and deliberately well above EuroPCR's 6% despite the shared hands-on character. Two things about this meeting pull in opposite directions. Against: it is substantially a procedural teaching meeting - ultrasound and cadaver workshops, problem-based learning, CME - which is exactly the EuroPCR shape where attendance says nothing about submitted science. For: the counted demographics show 346 trainees in a delegate body of 879, i.e. 39% residents and fellows, and trainees submit abstracts at far higher rates than any other group; the prospectus itself pitches the poster programme prominently - 'We invite medical providers of all backgrounds to submit abstracts to share your discoveries and knowledge with us. It is in our poster sessions that we will be introduced to the most leading-edge research.' A society that sells its poster hall to exhibitors as a headline feature has a poster hall worth selling. Denominator already discounted to 879 by removing the 131 industry/other.
